summary: Dengue outbreaks in the Philippines pose a significant public health threat, with over 271,000 cases and 1,100 deaths as of August 2019. The project aims to improve public health response by predicting dengue cases from climate and digital data and pinpointing possible hotspots from satellite data. This will enable public health and local government agencies to prioritize resources and take proactive measures to prevent outbreaks. The project targets public health officials and local government agencies in the Philippines, addressing the challenges of delayed dengue reporting and anticipating affected areas. By leveraging real-time climate, search, and satellite data, the project aims to reduce the impact of dengue outbreaks on vulnerable populations. The project's focus on disease surveillance and outbreak prediction aligns with efforts to strengthen health systems and improve disease management.
